speaker: SPK-01
name: Prof. Sharma (Host)
text: Good morning everyone. Welcome to today's session on Jupyter Notebook Markdown cells and structured documentation.

speaker: SPK-01
name: Prof. Sharma (Host)
text: In ordered lists, you give numbering to points and sub-points. Whereas in unordered lists, you use bullet symbols such as filled circles, filled squares, and empty circles.

speaker: SPK-02
name: Rahul Verma (CM-102941)
text: Professor, how does the Markdown renderer automatically differentiate a main point from a nested sub-point?

speaker: SPK-01
name: Prof. Sharma (Host)
text: Good question Rahul. When you indent sub-points with four spaces or a tab, the renderer changes the symbol—giving a filled circle to the main point, a square to sub-level 1, and an open circle to sub-level 2.

speaker: SPK-03
name: Ananya Patel (CM-108253)
text: Could you also show us how to insert hyperlinks to external documentation like Python.org?

speaker: SPK-01
name: Prof. Sharma (Host)
text: Certainly Ananya. In square brackets you write the clickable label text, and in parentheses immediately following, you provide the destination URL.

speaker: SPK-01
name: Prof. Sharma (Host)
text: For example, bracket 'Click here' followed by parenthesis 'https://python.org'. Once executed, the text displays with an underline and blue color indicating a valid hyperlink.

speaker: SPK-04
name: David Chen (CM-105190)
text: What is the syntax for embedding images, and what happens if the image address is broken or unavailable?

speaker: SPK-01
name: Prof. Sharma (Host)
text: The image syntax is identical to hyperlinks, but prefixed with an exclamation mark: exclamation mark, square brackets for alt text, and parentheses for the image URL.

speaker: SPK-01
name: Prof. Sharma (Host)
text: If the image address is not reachable, the descriptive text inside the square brackets will be displayed as fallback alt text.

speaker: SPK-02
name: Rahul Verma (CM-102941)
text: Can we embed multimedia like audio and video files using this same Markdown notation?

speaker: SPK-01
name: Prof. Sharma (Host)
text: Yes, multimedia files can be linked or embedded using standard HTML tags or Markdown tags within the notebook.

speaker: SPK-03
name: Ananya Patel (CM-108253)
text: Is there any assignment or task for this topic that we need to submit?

speaker: SPK-01
name: Prof. Sharma (Host)
text: Yes, everyone must practice creating a Markdown document with ordered lists, unordered lists, a hyperlink, and an image fallback. Please submit the notebook by Friday 5 PM.

speaker: SPK-04
name: David Chen (CM-105190)
text: Got it Professor, thank you! We will practice and submit the assignment on time.

speaker: SPK-01
name: Prof. Sharma (Host)
text: Great. Thank you all for participating actively. We will meet tomorrow at 10 AM for the next session. Have a great day!
